newsitem.title: USA: International tourists to U.S. at all-time high.
newsitem.headline: International tourists to U.S. at all-time high.

text.p: The number of international tourists visiting the United States hit an all-time high in 1996, the Commerce Department's Tourism Industries office announced on Monday.

About 46.3 million international travelers visited the United States last year, up seven percent from 1995. Last year's surge follows three consecutive years of declining tourism from outside the United States, the department said.

The increase can be partly attributed to improving economies in Canada and Mexico, two of the largest sources of visitors to the United States, Commerce reported. More than 15 million Canadian and nearly nine million Mexican tourists visited the United States in 1996.
"This is great news for the United States as tourism exports are a boon to a wide range of sectors in the U.S. economy," Commerce Secretary William Daley said in a statement.
Japan remained the leader in overseas tourists to the United States, with more than five million last year, followed by the United Kingdom, Germany, Brazil, South Korea, France and Italy.
About 57 million international travelers are expected to visit the United States in the year 2000, the Commerce Department said.
